109:class ConversationHandler(BaseHandler[Update, CCT, object]):
110:    """
111:    A handler to hold a conversation with a single or multiple users through Telegram updates by
112:    managing three collections of other handlers.
113:
114:    Warning:
115:        :class:`ConversationHandler` heavily relies on incoming updates being processed one by one.
116:        When using this handler, :attr:`telegram.ext.ApplicationBuilder.concurrent_updates` should
117:        be set to :obj:`False`.
118:
119:    Note:
120:        :class:`ConversationHandler` will only accept updates that are (subclass-)instances of
121:        :class:`telegram.Update`. This is, because depending on the :attr:`per_user` and
122:        :attr:`per_chat`, :class:`ConversationHandler` relies on
123:        :attr:`telegram.Update.effective_user` and/or :attr:`telegram.Update.effective_chat` in
124:        order to determine which conversation an update should belong to. For
125:        :attr:`per_message=True <per_message>`, :class:`ConversationHandler` uses
126:        :attr:`update.callback_query.message.message_id <telegram.Message.message_id>` when
127:        :attr:`per_chat=True <per_chat>` and
128:        :attr:`update.callback_query.inline_message_id <.CallbackQuery.inline_message_id>` when
129:        :attr:`per_chat=False <per_chat>`. For a more detailed explanation, please see our `FAQ`_.
130:
131:        Finally, :class:`ConversationHandler`, does *not* handle (edited) channel posts.
132:
133:    .. _`FAQ`: https://github.com/python-telegram-bot/python-telegram-bot/wiki\
134:        /Frequently-Asked-Questions#what-do-the-per_-settings-in-conversation handler-do
135:
136:    The first collection, a :obj:`list` named :attr:`entry_points`, is used to initiate the
137:    conversation, for example with a :class:`telegram.ext.CommandHandler` or
138:    :class:`telegram.ext.MessageHandler`.
139:
140:    The second collection, a :obj:`dict` named :attr:`states`, contains the different conversation
141:    steps and one or more associated handlers that should be used if the user sends a message when
142:    the conversation with them is currently in that state. Here you can also define a state for
143:    :attr:`TIMEOUT` to define the behavior when :attr:`conversation_timeout` is exceeded, and a
144:    state for :attr:`WAITING` to define behavior when a new update is received while the previous
145:    :attr:`block=False <block>` handler is not finished.
146:
147:    The third collection, a :obj:`list` named :attr:`fallbacks`, is used if the user is currently
148:    in a conversation but the state has either no associated handler or the handler that is
149:    associated to the state is inappropriate for the update, for example if the update contains a
150:    command, but a regular text message is expected. You could use this for a ``/cancel`` command
151:    or to let the user know their message was not recognized.
152:
153:    To change the state of conversation, the callback function of a handler must return the new
154:    state after responding to the user. If it does not return anything (returning :obj:`None` by
155:    default), the state will not change. If an entry point callback function returns :obj:`None`,
156:    the conversation ends immediately after the execution of this callback function.
157:    To end the conversation, the callback function must return :attr:`END` or ``-1``. To
158:    handle the conversation timeout, use handler :attr:`TIMEOUT` or ``-2``.
159:    Finally, :class:`telegram.ext.ApplicationHandlerStop` can be used in conversations as described
160:    in its documentation.
161:
162:    Note:
163:        In each of the described collections of handlers, a handler may in turn be a
164:        :class:`ConversationHandler`. In that case, the child :class:`ConversationHandler` should
165:        have the attribute :attr:`map_to_parent` which allows returning to the parent conversation
166:        at specified states within the child conversation.
167:
168:        Note that the keys in :attr:`map_to_parent` must not appear as keys in :attr:`states`
169:        attribute or else the latter will be ignored. You may map :attr:`END` to one of the parents
170:        states to continue the parent conversation after the child conversation has ended or even
171:        map a state to :attr:`END` to end the *parent* conversation from within the child
172:        conversation. For an example on nested :class:`ConversationHandler` s, see
173:        :any:`examples.nestedconversationbot`.
174:
175:    Examples:
176:        * :any:`Conversation Bot <examples.conversationbot>`
177:        * :any:`Conversation Bot 2 <examples.conversationbot2>`
178:        * :any:`Nested Conversation Bot <examples.nestedconversationbot>`
179:        * :any:`Persistent Conversation Bot <examples.persistentconversationbot>`
180:
181:    Args:
182:        entry_points (list[:class:`telegram.ext.BaseHandler`]): A list of :obj:`BaseHandler`
183:            objects that
184:            can trigger the start of the conversation. The first handler whose :meth:`check_update`
185:            method returns :obj:`True` will be used. If all return :obj:`False`, the update is not
186:            handled.
187:        states (dict[:obj:`object`, list[:class:`telegram.ext.BaseHandler`]]): A :obj:`dict` that
188:            defines the different states of conversation a user can be in and one or more
189:            associated :obj:`BaseHandler` objects that should be used in that state. The first
190:            handler whose :meth:`check_update` method returns :obj:`True` will be used.
191:        fallbacks (list[:class:`telegram.ext.BaseHandler`]): A list of handlers that might be used
192:            if the user is in a conversation, but every handler for their current state returned
193:            :obj:`False` on :meth:`check_update`. The first handler which :meth:`check_update`
194:            method returns :obj:`True` will be used. If all return :obj:`False`, the update is not
195:            handled.
196:        allow_reentry (:obj:`bool`, optional): If set to :obj:`True`, a user that is currently in a
197:            conversation can restart the conversation by triggering one of the entry points.
198:            Default is :obj:`False`.
199:        per_chat (:obj:`bool`, optional): If the conversation key should contain the Chat's ID.
200:            Default is :obj:`True`.
201:        per_user (:obj:`bool`, optional): If the conversation key should contain the User's ID.
202:            Default is :obj:`True`.
203:        per_message (:obj:`bool`, optional): If the conversation key should contain the Message's
204:            ID. Default is :obj:`False`.
205:        conversation_timeout (:obj:`float` | :obj:`datetime.timedelta`, optional): When this
206:            handler is inactive more than this timeout (in seconds), it will be automatically
207:            ended. If this value is ``0`` or :obj:`None` (default), there will be no timeout. The
208:            last received update and the corresponding :class:`context <.CallbackContext>` will be
209:            handled by *ALL* the handler's whose :meth:`check_update` method returns :obj:`True`
210:            that are in the state :attr:`ConversationHandler.TIMEOUT`.
211:
212:            Caution:
213:                * This feature relies on the :attr:`telegram.ext.Application.job_queue` being set
214:                  and hence requires that the dependencies that :class:`telegram.ext.JobQueue`
215:                  relies on are installed.
216:                * Using :paramref:`conversation_timeout` with nested conversations is currently
217:                  not supported. You can still try to use it, but it will likely behave
218:                  differently from what you expect.
219:
220:        name (:obj:`str`, optional): The name for this conversation handler. Required for
221:            persistence.
